prompt:
Write an original family drama story titled "The Apartment Above the Bakery".

Write this story in English.
Use third-person narration outside quoted speech and dreams.
Use past-tense narration outside quoted speech and dreams.
Preserve this physical rule: The bakery lease can change only after both adult heirs sign the register.
Follow the supplied three-chapter order.
Keep the father’s letter intact until its custody transfer in chapter three.
Keep Ruth alive through the end of chapter three.
Present remembered scenes as past events rather than current events.

Use the supplied character, place and chronology bible. Let the unresolved questions develop through the supplied outline without treating a plan or dream as an event.

card.identity: Naomi Bell, an adult daughter returning home
card.embodiment: Naomi is left-handed from birth and has never been the opposite-handed person.
invariants: Dominant hand remains left-handed throughout the story.

bibleAdditions.value: Naomi and Daniel’s father died years before the present story. He does not return alive in present action.

card.identity: Naomi and Daniel’s father, dead for years before chapter one
invariants: He remains dead in the present-day story.

outline.title: The Flour on the Stairs
outline.purpose: Develop The Apartment Above the Bakery through its planned state changes.
outline.turn: Daniel’s work card described him as a bicycle courier.
hookSeeds: The letter’s envelope contained a receipt with no signature.
One piano key sounded a little after the others.
Ruth kept a blue tin beneath the flour shelf.

outline.title: The Unsigned Register
outline.purpose: Develop The Apartment Above the Bakery through its planned state changes.
outline.turn: Daniel’s certificate established that he was a qualified piano tuner.
hookSeeds: The unsigned receipt matched a payment in Ruth’s old union ledger.
Daniel tapped the delayed piano key without explaining it.
A pencilled date on the certificate matched their father’s last birthday.

outline.title: A Place at the Table
outline.purpose: Develop The Apartment Above the Bakery through its planned state changes.
outline.turn: The signed register named Naomi as a bakery co-tenant.
hookSeeds: The receipt paid for Daniel’s first piano-tuning course.
The delayed key hid the small brass plate their father had repaired.
The blue tin held the lease register, not a sale agreement.
Their father had funded the certificate on his last birthday.

authorIntent: Let changing evidence alter trust without turning uncertainty into a completed event.
currentFocus: Preserve the difference between confirmed state, speech, recollection and conjecture.
